q: My white titles disappear over a busy, bright background. How do I make them readable without a big ugly box?
a: 1. On the text layer add a soft shadow or a thin dark stroke (`graphics.set` with shadow / stroke). 2. If it still fights the picture, a subtle shape layer behind the text, pinned so it fits the words (`graphics.pin`), with lowered opacity. 3. Or darken the area under the title a little on the grade with a soft window. 4. Avoid thin fonts over moving footage: they flicker after compression.

q: title readable on some shots and not others in the same scene
a: Keep one treatment for the whole title (shadow or stroke strong enough for the brightest shot) rather than restyling per shot; or move the title to a calmer part of the frame, inside the safe margins.

q: Text over a moving crowd shimmers after upload.
a: Thin strokes and small serif fonts flicker after compression: use a heavier weight, a larger size and a soft shadow; check the exported file, not only the timeline.

q: How do I make English, Spanish and German versions of the same explainer video?
a: 1. Finish and lock the English edit. 2. Duplicate the sequence per language so each keeps its own copy. 3. Swap the narration: record or create each language's narration (`tts.create` with a voice for that language) on the narration track; music and effects stay. 4. Captions per language as their own caption track (`captions.import` of a translated file, or edit a copy). 5. Replace on-screen text in the graphics, then queue all versions for export (`export.queue.add`, `export.queue.start`).

q: German narration is longer than the English one and runs over the next scene
a: Shorten the script (`tts.edit` keeps the clip's place), speed the voice up slightly, or open small gaps in the picture for that version; never let the narration cross a scene change that matters.

q: Keep the titles editable so translating them is quick.
a: Build the titles as graphics templates with only the text editable, pinned shapes that grow with longer words (`graphics.pin`), so each language's version only needs the text changed.

q: How do I make a split-screen duet video of two singers who recorded separately?
a: 1. Both clips on the timeline, one on V1 and one on V2. 2. Sync them by the music in their audio (`clip.synchronize` by audio), or by a clap / marker. 3. Split screen: Crop the V2 clip to half and Position each singer in their half. 4. Mix: both voices centred or panned slightly apart, levels matched with Auto-Match, one clean backing track under them.

q: duet: one singer's video drifts a little behind over the song
a: Split their clip at a pause (`sequence.addEdit`) and re-align the second half to the backing track by ear and waveform, or adjust its speed a hair with Speed / Duration.

q: The two singers' videos look totally different in colour.
a: Grade one, grab a still and Shot Match the other to it (`grade.shotMatch`), matching skin first; then a shared look on both.

q: How do I add a translated voice-over on top of an interview, like on the news?
a: 1. Record the translation as a voice-over on its own track (`audio.voiceover.start`) or make it with Text to Speech. 2. Let the original voice play alone for a second, then start the translation and duck the original far under it (`essentialSound.generateDucking`, or Volume keyframes with the Audio Clip Mixer). 3. Bring the original back up briefly at the end of each answer. 4. Type the translation Dialogue and keep it centred.

q: translated voice and original voice sound muddy together
a: Duck the original lower under the translation and keep the translation dry and close; Clean Up Voice on the translation (`audio.cleanupVoice`) evens its level.

q: Voice-over translation or subtitles for an interview: which is better?
a: Subtitles keep the speaker's real voice and are cheaper to make (captions from the transcript, translated); a voice-over suits viewers who can't read along or short news pieces. Both: subtitles as a separate file next to the dubbed version.

q: How do I give each speaker's captions a different colour?
a: 1. Put each speaker's captions on their own caption track: import one file per speaker (`captions.import`: each arrives as a new caption track), or add a track per speaker by hand (`captions.newTrack`, `captions.add`). 2. Style each track with its colour (`captions.setStyle` with `color`), keeping the same font and size. A newly imported track becomes C1 and the earlier ones move down, so check which speaker is on which track (`captions.list`) before styling. 3. Check contrast against the picture; an outline or background helps.

q: coloured caption for each person but yellow is hard to read on a sunny shot
a: Give the track an outline (`captions.setStyle` with `outline` and `outlineColor`) or a semi-transparent background (`background`, `backgroundColor`), so any colour reads over bright shots.

q: Speaker colours in captions for YouTube as a separate file.
a: A sidecar file (SRT especially) carries little or no styling, so colours are likely lost: name the speaker in the caption text (`captions.setText`) for the file, or burn the coloured captions into the video for social clips.
